summary: Rule-clean, but the size of the win rests on a router side branch of ~80-90 us that the current master profile does not show. At turn_1 sliding the router pair is 32.0 us for 2 calls, under a ~52 us pooler plus a 7 us norm. The realistic effect is SM-contention relief of ~0.3-0.7% on the geomean, inside the ~1.5% run-to-run drift. With 1 prefill check left today, it should not use that check: the turn loads now trail SGLang (0.93-0.98x) because of the Triton expert GEMM, which is a bigger and resolvable lever.
justification: Mechanism: folding the hi/lo router (512 extra output rows) into the pooler GEMM over the same ffn_input is sound on H200. It removes two split-K nvjet_tss launches, a splitKreduce and the stream fork/join, and a 4608-wide cuBLAS tile GEMM should run the router's 6.3 GFLOP at turn_1 at ~700+ TFLOP/s (~8-9 us) instead of ~190 TFLOP/s (32 us). Profile on master (b33b87b5083b4d1c): turn_1 sliding shows nvjet_tss_64x96 splitK at 32.0 us/2 calls. The pooler is one of the three nvjet_128x192 calls (156.0 us total, ~52 us each), so the main branch is ~59 us and the side branch (32 us + reduce + FusedMuseSparkRouting, ~40 us) already fits under it. The 81.8 us splitK row on turn_1 full, for an identical M and identical router code, is wait time folded into an overlapping kernel's row (the profiler says rows include waits), not work. That is the same conclusion the router-triton-hilo-splitk-turn review reached. So the prize is not the claimed ~35-40 us removed from the critical path. It is the router SM-time no longer competing with the pooler: ~32 us of router SM-time replaced by ~6-8 us of extra pooler GEMM plus a ~3-5 us cast/slice-add, i.e. ~15-20 us at turn_1 (~1.5% of the 1141 us sliding shape). At turn_4, 131 us of router is replaced by ~25-30 us of GEMM plus ~15-20 us of cast/add, ~60-80 us out of 3435/4975 us (~2%). The spec expects turn_4 flat, but it is plausibly the better load. In load terms (TASK.md weights 46/16, geomean over 3 loads, first_turn flat by its gate), that is ~0.3-0.5% from turn_1 plus ~0.6% from turn_4: ~0.5-1% headline. One run cannot resolve that (LESSONS: ~1.5-2.5% per-shape drift). The concat GEMM's own row is readable in top_kernels, but the per-shape deltas will not be. Weakest link: the inherited '80-90 us side branch on the critical path' premise. Second risk: the extra fp32 output write (14 MB at T=753, 55 MB at T=3012) and cuBLAS choosing a different, possibly worse, algorithm for the fp32-out N=4608 GEMM than for the bf16-out N=4096 pooler.
confounders: sglang-pipeline-parity: it is the base that provides the side-stream fork this change removes. It is not separable: reverting its patch removes the fork, the router path and the whole pipeline together, so there is no A/B against it. The change's effect depends only on how much the forked router overlaps the pooler, which this base fixes.

experts-triton-w4a16-first-turn-blockt256 (with stage 2 under it): it does not touch the router, pooler or fork, and its first_turn-only tile change sits behind the same >4096 gate this hypothesis leaves on the parity path, so there is no interaction at first_turn. At turn shapes it replaced Marlin with the Triton expert GEMM, which now runs 847 us at turn_1 sliding vs Marlin's 730 us and leaves turn loads at 0.93-0.98x of SGLang. That changes nothing about the router/pooler overlap, but it lowers this hypothesis's priority. A later gate back to Marlin at the turn shapes would change the denominator (shape time), not the absolute saving.
interference: No companion is warranted, and the parent itself should wait. ab-revert has no meaningful target: reverting parity removes the fork entirely, and reverting the expert rewrite does not touch this path. ab-tune of the landed fork would be the sibling router-triton-hilo-splitk-turn (held), which is a different engine for the same limiter, not a tuning of a landed change. A control isolating a sub-change, for example the concat GEMM with the fork kept, would need its own check to resolve an effect that is already below one run's resolution. When it does run, it can be attributed without a companion: the tss splitK rows and the splitKreduce should vanish, the pooler-sized nvjet should grow by about 12% (more means cuBLAS picked a worse fp32-out algorithm), and first_turn is a built-in control. The headline cannot be attributed from one run either way, and with 1 check left today a companion is out of the question.
rules_flags: None that break a rule. The router hi+lo BF16 split with FP32 accumulation is explicitly allowed (TASK.md Weights). w_cat is a lossless repack in prepare() and keeps the BF16 pooler rows unchanged.
Pooler activations: computing the pooler in fp32 and rounding to BF16 before the pre-expert norm keeps BF16 where SGLang does. Only cuBLAS accumulation order differs, which is fine.

The gate on tokens <= 4096 is a shape branch, which is allowed. There are no host syncs. y and the slices are graph-pool allocations. The strided y[:, :4096] cast and the y[:, 4096:4352] + y[:, 4352:4608] add are ordinary graph nodes.
If FusedMuseSparkRouting needs contiguous logits, the slice-add already produces a contiguous [T, 256] tensor. Confirm the routing kernel accepts it as is, without an extra copy.
open_questions: Is the router branch on the turn critical path at all? On master, turn_1 sliding has the router at 32 us vs a ~52 us pooler plus a 7 us norm. Only a per-call trace (the profile json) would settle it, and if it is off the path the turn_1 'up to 35-40 us' is at most ~15-20 us of contention relief.
Turn_4 may be the better load (131 us of router SM-time vs ~45 us added), contrary to the 'flat' expectation. Should the expected block be revised before any future run?

Priority: master's turn shapes are now 0.93-0.98x of SGLang because the Triton expert GEMM is slower than Marlin at T=753/3012. Gating the turn shapes back to Marlin, or a turn-shape stage of the rewrite, is a ~5-7% per-shape lever. Should prefill's last check go there instead?

When quota is plentiful, run this and router-triton-hilo-splitk-turn as a pair on the same day. They target the same branch and do not stack, so pairing them makes the router-row times comparable even though the headlines are unresolvable.
